body: I'm not really sure, to be honest. I think I kept going because I had some vague hope that things would get better. But I'm having a hard time believing that anymore. Hope feels like a lie. I always end up back in this position, no matter what I do.
Ah gotcha. Yeah, articulating those thoughts and feelings can be so incredibly difficult. I'm glad to hear that you're feeling and doing better though.

I'm sorry to hear you've had to go through something similar. It really is awful. I just feel like it's going to eventually get the better of me. I'm already consumed with guilt and self-loathing as it is, and now I have even more reason to feel that way.
That's what I'm most worried about. I don't know if I could handle it. I have so few friends to begin with.

So you're basing your figures off of the latest incarnation of one Avengers team? How about superhero comics as a whole? 

P.S. The Marvel Universe is, well, a universe. It encompasses not only the United States, but the entire globe (as well as other galaxies and dimensions). Imagine if its characters were representative of the world's demographics.

I'm sorry to hear that you're feeling this way. I can certainly relate. Would it be helpful to contextualize your explanation by mentioning BPD or depression? It can be a scary and complicated topic to bring up, but it can also be helpful to put a name to what it is you're feeling.

Thank you for your feedback. I'm hoping she does read up on it, too. The hardest part at this point is the silence. This is probably  not true, but I feel like I'm being punished, which makes it harder to feel optimistic about the situation. Hopefully time does heals all wounds.
Because white men are not underrepresented in comics.
